lessons.title: let, run, with, apply, also — The Real Decision Rule
lessons.content: The choice isn't stylistic - it's about what you need back and how you refer to the object. Use `apply` when configuring an object and you want the object itself back (this-reference, returns receiver) - e.g. building a view. Use `also` for side effects like logging where you want the object back but refer to it as `it` for clarity. Use `let` to transform a value or run null-safe code, returning the lambda's result. Use `run` when you need both a this-reference AND a different return value. Use `with` when the object isn't nullable and you're not chaining.

lessons.title: Common Anti-Patterns: Nested Scope Functions
lessons.content: Overusing scope functions - especially nesting them (`a.let { b.also { ... it.run { ... } } }`) - hurts readability more than it helps, and makes `this`/`it` references ambiguous. A good rule from real codebases: if you can't tell what `it` refers to without scrolling up, refactor to a named variable or a regular function instead. Scope functions are for concise, single-purpose blocks - not for replacing well-named functions.
